probes.question: A lily doubles every day and covers half the pond on day 29. When is the pond fully covered?
True or false: with daily doubling, the lily covers a quarter of the pond the day before it covers half.

image.alt: Claude Monet's painting of a pond covered with water lilies beneath a footbridge.
image.credit: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926) / Art Institute of Chicago

panels.text: A riddle French children are given: a water lily grows in a pond, and the plant doubles in size every day.
Left alone, it would smother the pond in 30 days, killing the other living things in the water.
Day after day the plant looks small, so people decide not to worry until it covers half the pond.
Which day is that? The 29th, which leaves only one day to save the pond. Doubling feels slow, then suddenly it is not.
